valdosaurus:eswiki:3.title: Valdosaurus canaliculatus (Historia de la investigación y clasificación)

facts.statement: The only valid species of Valdosaurus is V. canaliculatus.
facts.quote: species: canaliculatus

facts.statement: Valdosaurus is a bipedal, herbivorous dryosaurid dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous of the Isle of Wight and other parts of England.
facts.quote: Valdosaurus ("Weald lizard") is a genus of bipedal herbivorous dryosaurid dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous of the Isle of Wight and elsewhere in England.

facts.statement: In 1889, Richard Lydekker assigned the remains to Camptosaurus valdensis based on a partial lower jaw and other bones.
facts.quote: In 1889, Richard Lydekker assigned them to Camptosaurus, alongside a partial lower jaw, and applied the name Camptosaurus valdensis.

facts.statement: Rev. William Fox collected two small femora near Cowleaze Chine on the Isle of Wight in the 19th century.
facts.quote: At some point in the 19th century, the Rev. William Fox collected two small femora (upper leg bones) near Cowleaze Chine on the south-west coast of the Isle of Wight.

facts.statement: The species name valdensis is derived from the Old English word 'weald', referring to the Weald area.
facts.quote: The species name, valdensis derives from valdo, a modification of the Old English word weald ("a wood") which refers to the Weald area.

facts.statement: In 1975, Peter Galton assigned the femora to Dryosaurus canaliculatus after concluding they did not belong to Camptosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1975, Galton re-examined the femora, and concluded that they did not belong to Camptosaurus. He therefore assigned them to Dryosaurus, and applied the name Dryosaurus canaliculatus.

facts.statement: Galton and Philippe Taquet described a second species, V. nigeriensis, from Niger in 1982.
facts.quote: A second species, V. nigeriensis, was described by Galton and Philippe Taquet from younger rocks from Niger in 1982.

facts.statement: In 2009, Peter Galton concluded that fossils from outside England could not be reliably assigned to Valdosaurus and reclassified V. nigeriensis as Elrhazosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2009, Galton reviewed the Valdosaurus material. He concluded that no fossils from outside England could be reliably referred to the genus. He thus gave V. nigeriensis its own genus: Elrhazosaurus.

facts.statement: Nick Chase discovered a new Valdosaurus specimen in Compton Bay on the Isle of Wight in 2012, with the exact location withheld to prevent theft.
facts.quote: In 2012, a new specimen of Valdosaurus was discovered, in Compton Bay on the Isle of Wight, by Nick Chase; the exact location of its discovery has been withheld to prevent attempts to steal material from the site.

facts.statement: While type specimens were small (14 cm femur, 10 kg), larger specimens like the Compton Bay find may have reached 4 meters in length and 400 kg in mass.
facts.quote: Whereas the type specimens were very small, with a femur (thigh bone) length of just 14 cm and an estimated body mass of 10 kg, larger specimens such as the Compton specimen may have reached body lengths of around 4 m and body masses of roughly 400 kg.

facts.statement: Valdosaurus caudal vertebrae have lengthened, backswept neural spines that overhang more than one following vertebra, a trait distinct from other ornithischians.
facts.quote: The caudal vertebrae of Valdosaurus differ from those of other ornithischians in that the vertebrae in the middle of the caudal series have neural spines (the tall, dorsal/upper midline structures) which are lengthened and backswept to such an extent that each overhangs more than one postceding vertebra.

facts.statement: Unlike other dryosaurids, Valdosaurus canaliculatus has an open obturator notch on the pubis.
facts.quote: In other dryosaurids, the obturator notch on the pubis (to which certain obturator muscles attached) is closed, but in V. canaliculatus, it is open.

facts.statement: It is debated whether many English specimens, including cranial elements and teeth, truly belong to Valdosaurus.
facts.quote: Even where many of the English specimens were concerned it was uncertain whether they belonged to Valdosaurus, including all cranial elements and teeth.

facts.statement: The presence of Valdosaurus in Spain remains questionable.
facts.quote: Records from Spain remain questionable.

facts.statement: Valdosaurus is generally classified as a member of the family Dryosauridae.
facts.quote: Today Valdosaurus is generally considered a member of the Dryosauridae.

facts.statement: Peter Galton originally assigned Valdosaurus to the paraphyletic family Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: Galton assigned Valdosaurus to the Hypsilophodontidae, using an older and broader definition, wherein it is paraphyletic.

facts.statement: The genus Valdosaurus was established by Peter Galton in 1977.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Galton, 1977

facts.statement: The species Valdosaurus canaliculatus was named by Peter Galton in 1975.
facts.quote: species_authority: Galton, 1975

facts.statement: Reverend William Darwin Fox collected two small femurs near Cowleaze Chine on the southwest coast of the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: En el el reverendo William Darwin Fox recolectó dos pequeños fémures cerca de Cowleaze Chine en la costa suroeste de la isla de Wight.

facts.statement: Peter Galton named the femurs as a new species of Dryosaurus, Dryosaurus canaliculatus, in 1975.
facts.quote: En 1975 Peter Galton los nombró como una nueva especie de Dryosaurus, Dryosaurus canaliculatus.

facts.statement: Peter Galton created the new genus Valdosaurus for this species in 1977.
facts.quote: En 1977 Galton creó un nuevo género para esta especie: Valdosaurus

facts.statement: A second species, V. nigeriensis, was described by Galton and Philippe Taquet from rocks in Niger in 1982.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, V. nigeriensis, fue descrita por Galton y Philippe Taquet de rocas más recientes de Níger en 1982

facts.statement: In 1998, William Blows inadvertently created the name Valdosaurus dextrapoda, but it was an error and the species was never justified.
facts.quote: En 1998 William Blows inadvertidamente creó otra especie del género, Valdosaurus dextrapoda, al incluir este nombre en una lisa de fauna, pero esto fue un error, y la especie nunca ha sido justificada.

facts.statement: A new specimen of Valdosaurus was described in 2016.
facts.quote: En 2016 se describió un nuevo ejemplar de Valdosaurus.

facts.statement: Valdosaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately between 130 and 125 million years ago in the Barremian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico hace aproximadamnete entre 130 a 125 millones de años durante el Barremiense

facts.statement: Valdosaurus lived in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Valdosaurus fossils have been found on the Isle of Wight and other parts of England.
facts.quote: Fue hallado en la isla de Wight y otras partes de Inglaterra.

facts.statement: The rock units where Valdosaurus fossils were found were deposited between the Berriasian and Barremian, approximately 145 to 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: Estas unidades rocosas fueron depositadas entre las épocas del Berriasiense al Barremiense, hace aproximadamente 145 a 125 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype femurs belonged to a juvenile individual, while an adult would be a medium-sized euornithopod with femurs reaching half a meter in length.
facts.quote: pero estos eran de un individuo juvenil y que un adulto en cambio sería un "euornitópodo de tamaño mediano", con fémures que alcanzan una longitud de medio metro.

facts.statement: In life, the newly described specimen would have measured around 4 to 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: En vida, el espécimen habría medido alrededor de 4 a 5 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Sedimentological data suggests the depositional environment of the Wessex Formation was a floodplain intersected by river and lake deposits.
facts.quote: Sedimentological data suggests that the depositional environment of the Wessex Formation was a floodplain intersected by fluvial (river) and lacustrine (lake) deposits.

facts.statement: Burned plant and insect material and fusain suggest that the environment experienced frequent wildfires.
facts.quote: Burned plant and insect material and fusain suggests that the environment experienced frequent wildfires

facts.statement: It is uncertain whether many of the English specimens truly belong to Valdosaurus, including all cranial material and teeth.
facts.quote: Incluso es incierto si muchos de los especímenes ingleses realmente pertenecen a Valdosaurus, incluyendo todo el material craneano y los dientes.

facts.statement: The genus Valdosaurus was named by Galton in 1977.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Valdosaurus (genus), Galton 1977

facts.statement: Valdosaurus belongs to the family Dryosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Dryosauridae

facts.statement: Valdosaurus is classified within the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Valdosaurus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Aptian stages, between 154.8 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Aptian (154.8 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 12 recorded fossil occurrences of Valdosaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 12

rejected.statement: Peter Galton reclassified the remains as a new species of Dryosaurus in 1975 and later as the new genus and species Valdosaurus canaliculatus.
rejected.quote: In the 1970s, Peter Galton reassigned these remains to a new species of Dryosaurus, then to an entirely new genus and species, that being Valdosaurus proper.

rejected.statement: In 1977, Peter Galton established the new genus Valdosaurus for the remains previously assigned to Dryosaurus.
rejected.quote: Two years later, Galton recognised that they were in fact morphologically distinct from Dryosaurus, and erected a new genus for them, Valdosaurus.

rejected.statement: Valdosaurus lived between approximately 145 and 125 million years ago during the Berriasian and Barremian stages.
rejected.quote: These rock units were deposited between the Berriasian and Barremian stages, between approximately 145 and 125 million years ago.

rejected.statement: The holotype femurs are small, measuring 14 centimeters in length, which led to an estimated total length of 1.2 meters and a weight of 10 kilograms.

rejected.statement: Much of the flora consisted of low ground cover primarily of pteridophytes, with occasional stands of conifers, cycads, and the tree fern Tempskya.
rejected.quote: Much of the flora of the formed of low ground cover, consisting primarily of pteridophytes, with occasional stands of conifers, cycads and the tree fern Tempskya.

rejected.quote: Por tanto dio a V. nigeriensis su propio género, Elrhazosaurus.
